# WorkstationNL dense control: the dark splitter fails the :active read on press

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` — "the real tour keeps density, data, Canvas output, themes, rails, and identities live" — reds deterministically at `:1294`: `expect(darkDockActive.horizontal.active, 'the real dark-mode splitter owns the active pointer target').toBe(true)` receives `false`. Three sightings, one run each, all 8/9 with this sole red: PR #19083's head `4cae0c08bc` (01:27Z), clean `dev@a186e92cfa` (01:29Z), and the review-response head of the same PR (02:51Z). Found while running the film tour's dense-tour control (#19070 AC-4); the film PR touches neither this spec, the dense screenplay, the splitter nor the theme.

## The Problem

The light-mode arm at `:1164` reads the same probe — `readDockChrome` (`:364`) returns `element.matches(':active')` for `.neo-dashboard-dock-split-horizontal > .neo-dashboard-dock-splitter-horizontal` — after the same `mouse.move` + `mouse.down`, and passes. The dark arm at `:1294`, later in the same test, fails. The engine's active paint contract (`resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss:456`: `&:active` background, ring and handle tokens) is therefore not the difference; something about the second press is. Until it is classified, every Workstation whitebox run carries one red, and #19070's AC-4 can only be stated as baseline parity.

## The Architectural Reality

- The probe reads the UA pseudo-class, not an engine class: `:active` holds only while the pressed pointer's target chain includes the splitter. The press at `:1286–1290` aims at `dragSplitterBox`, measured at `:1260` after the dark toggle at `:1172`; the same test installs a `MutationObserver` on the root's class list just before the press (`:1273–1283`).
- `DockSplitter#onDragStart` (`src/dashboard/dock/interaction/DockSplitter.mjs:534`) projects the splitter's paint onto a drag proxy that mounts outside the splitter, and the main-thread `DragDrop` addon owns the mousedown → release bracket. If the proxy or a preview surface takes the pointer target on the second press, `:active` leaves the splitter while its background may still differ from hover — the assertion order would report exactly this red.
- #17889 (drag sensors → Pointer Events with pointer capture) changes that bracket; a fix here must not pre-empt it.

## Classification (2026-09-23, instrumented runs 08:48–09:13Z on the seat's own bridge per #19066)

**(b) target taken — by the theme toggle's view transition, not a drag proxy.** At the dark press, `document.elementsFromPoint(x, y)` at the splitter's centre returned only `<html>` while the splitter was connected with its box exactly where it was measured (`live` = `measured`); the pressed chain was `[html]`. `Workspace#toggleWorkspaceTheme` (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:685`) runs `DomAccess.startViewTransition` with a 100 ms capture window and a 500 ms circular reveal (`src/main/DomAccess.mjs:1143`, `src/main/DomUtils.mjs:82`), and while the transition runs its `::view-transition` pseudo-tree owns hit-testing: at the press the `::view-transition-group/old/new(root)` animations stood at t = 100 ms, and the splitter became hit-testable 394–415 ms later. So `:active` never reached the splitter and the drag never started — the later `the user drag commits a semantic resizeSplit document change` assertion read a delta of 0. The light arm passed only because its unrelated 1.2 s listener-readiness wait outlasts the reveal. The proxy hypothesis was falsified: no `[class*="proxy"]` element existed at either press.

Once the press landed, the tour ran further than it had in weeks and unmasked three more layers, each classified: **(2)** the monitor counted every `.neo-tab-header-toolbar` under the root (8), but each rail's `RevealOverlay` composes a runtime-only `tab.header.Toolbar` (idle-hidden, zero rect, in the DOM from boot) — a test premise, fixed by scoping to the containers' own headers; **(3)** one sampled frame during `splitNode(security → below scale)` shows two visible overflow controls, the newborn single-tab Security container's beside the heavy group's — deterministic, engine, filed as #19094; **(4)** `dark splitter active feedback is distinct from hover` red 1 in 3 because the splitter's `background-color` transitions over `--dock-transition-duration-fast` (120 ms, `Container.scss:395`) and both reads could catch the colour being left — fixed by settling the four hover/active reads on `getAnimations().length === 0`; **(5)** the Canvas receipt (`the exact scale Canvas changes after its worker receives new data`) reds in 5 of 9 runs with the App-worker `values` changed and the same, still-transferred canvas node never repainting — captured as a defect-note (09:14Z), mechanism unknown, falsified as unrelated to a held press.

## The Fix

Both presses wait until a hit test at the splitter's centre returns the splitter (`expectSplitterUnderPointer`), so the dark arm keeps its honest `:active` read; the four hover/active colour reads settle first (`readSettledDockChrome`); the tour monitor tracks `.neo-tab-container > .neo-tab-header-toolbar`; the duplicate-overflow sample names a control's real toolbar via `closest()` (the control is the toolbar's own action contribution). Test-only; no engine change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 The cause is classified from the instrumented read (stale box / target taken / engine gap) and recorded here.
- [ ] AC-2 The dark-mode press lands on the splitter and its drag commits a `resizeSplit` document change — the arm's `:active` read and its active-vs-hover colour read pass in three consecutive runs on `dev`. *Restated 2026-09-23 after classification: the original 9/9 target is blocked by two reds this fix unmasked, #19094 (deterministic, engine) and the Canvas receipt flake (defect-note), both classified with owners and not this ticket's.*
- [ ] AC-3 The light-mode arm keeps its meaning (a press shows the active feedback); no assertion is removed without a replacement.

## Out of Scope

- #17889's sensor migration.
- The film tour (#19070 / PR #19083), which only reports this red as its control's baseline.
- #19094 (the newborn container's one-frame overflow control) and the Canvas receipt flake — unmasked here, owned elsewhere.
